result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_assortativity_nominal()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate assortativity for categorical (nominal) node attributes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L28927-L29015){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_assortativity_nominal(attribute) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Nominal assortativity](/assets/graphs/get-assortativity-nominal.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles joined by one edge, with the nodes split into two categories: A, B, C in the accent color and D, E, F in teal. Six of the seven edges join nodes of the same category, so mixing is assortative and r = 0.714." width="100%"} Measures the tendency of nodes with the same attribute value to connect, also known as homophily. Uses Newman's formula for categorical mixing patterns. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the categorical node attribute to analyze. Must exist on all nodes as a node attribute. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Assortativity coefficient in range `[-1, 1]`: - `r = 1`: perfect assortativity (only same-type connections) - `r > 0`: assortative (same types prefer to connect) - `r = 0`: random mixing - `r < 0`: disassortative (different types prefer to connect) ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If attribute doesn't exist on all nodes, graph has no edges, or there are fewer than two different attribute values. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For a categorical attribute this is Newman's *modularity by attribute*: $r = \dfrac{\mathrm{tr}(E) - \|E^2\|_1}{1 - \|E^2\|_1}$, where $E$ is the mixing matrix whose entries $e_{ij}$ record the fraction of edges running between attribute values $i$ and $j$. $r = 1$ means the graph is fully segregated by attribute (only within-class edges); $r = 0$ matches random mixing at the given marginals; negative $r$ signals systematic cross-class connections. This is the tool that formalizes the "birds of a feather" intuition, and negative variants surface bipartite-style structures like predator-prey webs or user-item recommendation graphs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} When most edges connect nodes that share the same categorical attribute (students to students, faculty to faculty), the assortativity coefficient is positive -- a sign of homophily: ::: {#5165e2d5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node("Alice", group="students") .add_node("Bob", group="students") .add_node("Carol", group="students") .add_node("Prof1", group="faculty") .add_node("Prof2", group="faculty") .add_edge("Alice", "Bob") .add_edge("Bob", "Carol") .add_edge("Prof1", "Prof2") .add_edge("Alice", "Prof1") # One cross-group edge ) # Returns a positive value: mostly within-group connections g.get_assortativity_nominal("group") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.4666666666666667 ``` ::: ::: Predator-prey relationships show the opposite pattern: predators connect to prey rather than to each other, producing a negative coefficient: ::: {#c90a251b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node("Wolf", type="predator") .add_node("Lion", type="predator") .add_node("Deer", type="prey") .add_node("Rabbit", type="prey") .add_edge("Wolf", "Deer") .add_edge("Wolf", "Rabbit") .add_edge("Lion", "Deer") ) # Returns a negative value: predators connect to prey, not each other g.get_assortativity_nominal("type") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: :::
